author: Souter
authority: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela, a member of the judgment coalition, assigns this lead opinion.
form: Form fixed before authorship or balance counts: one signed opinion of the Court after plenary merits submission. Corporate coverage and application of the punishment inquiry are related propositions in one constitutional adjudication with a common full-rationale coalition; they do not justify separate leads or a summary disposition.
reason: Fit governs because all nine already support the complete constitutional rule and remedy, and no accommodation is needed. Souter's frozen application separates the enacted fault judgment and complete retrospective command from mere identification or legitimate ratepayer protection. That supplies the precise functional work this opinion requires while preserving the challenger's burden and ordinary prudence regulation. Stevens is the strongest alternative through his Ambassador Books opinion; both have the same low count and can carry the rule. Souter's direct treatment of the combination of culpability, financial consequence and absent adjudication fits this distinct application. Stone's approved coverage analysis is fully compatible but supplies no necessary accommodation or authorship advantage over that lower-count choice. Assignment changes no ground, join or remedy.
